title: The static and final Keywords Together
subtopics: Distinguishing reference immutability from object immutability
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of the static and final keywords together and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—constants—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study the static and final keywords together with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you model valid object state and expose behavior without leaking implementation details. In this lesson, focus on constants and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A class defines state and behavior; an object is an instance. Use constructors to establish valid state and encapsulation to keep the object’s invariants true as it changes. Apply that reasoning specifically to constants and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

items.title: Immutable references
items.text: A reference identifies an object; assigning a reference copies the reference value, not the whole object. Two variables may therefore refer to the same mutable object.
